Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said that he is willing to wait to have kids till Elon Musk’s Neuralink ...
Article Text:
Why Alexandr Wang wants to wait for Neuralink before having kids

Why Alexandr Wang believes children could adapt better

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces such as Elon Musk’s Neuralink become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year while discussing the future of AI, human development and brain-computer interfaces. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids. “I want to wait to have kids until we figure out how Neuralink or other … start working,” Alexandr Wang said during the podcast.Wang’s reason is linked to how he believes children’s brains could adapt to the technology. During the podcast, he explained that the first several years of a child’s life are an important period for brain development. He argued that the high level of neuroplasticity during childhood could allow children who grow up with brain-computer interfaces to use the technology in ways that adults may not be able to.“In your first like seven years of life, your brain is more neuroplastic than at any other point in your life, like by an order of magnitude,” Wang said.He then compared the idea with how children develop their ability to process information from their senses.Alexandr Wang described a case involving children born with cataracts. He said that if the cataracts prevent a child from seeing during the early years of development, removing them later may not allow the child to develop normal vision because the brain did not learn to process signals from the eyes during the key period.His view is that a similar effect could eventually apply to brain-computer interfaces. “When we get Neuralink and we get these other technologies, kids who are born with them are going to learn how to use them in like, crazy, crazy ways,” Wang said.Wang said a brain-computer interface could eventually become integrated into the way a person's brain works if it is introduced early enough. He believes this could be different for adults who receive an implant later in life.“It'll be a actually like a part of their brain in a way that it'll never be true for an adult who gets like a neural link or whatever, hooked into their brain,” he said.The Meta AI chief also connected his thinking about brain-computer interfaces to the rapid development of artificial intelligence. “I believe a lot in AI,” Wang said, adding that he expects AI to become “smarter and smarter, more and more capable, more and more powerful.”He said AI could eventually take different forms, including robots and other systems.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids.

Article Title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison’s first wife filed for divorce 3 months after their daughter's birth; but he was 'determined to remain friends' as ...
Article Text:
Larry Ellison's reflection on the split

Life after the divorce

Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. According to a report by People.com, the split came at a pivotal time in Ellison’s life as he was balancing the early growth of Oracle with the new family responsibilities. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983. Their son, David, was born in January of that year, followed three years later by their daughter, Megan, born January 31, 1986.Barbara filed for divorce in April 1986, just three months after Megan's birth, bringing the three-year marriage to an end.In Matthew Symonds' 2003 book "Softwar: An Intimate Portrait of Larry Ellison and Oracle," Ellison said he was determined to remain friends with his ex-wife for the sake of raising healthy, happy children. He also reflected on how fatherhood had reshaped him personally, saying becoming a father fundamentally changed his personality, made him more sensitive to his children's needs and feelings, and gradually made him a more considerate friend and partner more broadly. He described the experience simply as growing up.After the split, Barbara took over the role of primary caregiver, raising David and Megan largely away from the spotlight of Ellison's rapidly growing tech fortune.She instilled in both children an early love of film, reportedly building a collection of more than 3,000 VHS tapes that the siblings would watch repeatedly, including favorites like "Jurassic Park" and "Back to the Future."That shared love of movies would go on to shape both siblings' adult careers. David Ellison founded Skydance Media, the production company behind franchises including "Mission: Impossible" and "Top Gun: Maverick." Megan Ellison founded Annapurna Pictures, which has produced acclaimed films such as "Zero Dark Thirty," "Her," and "American Hustle," earning her multiple Academy Award nominations along the way.Ellison, now one of the world’s wealthiest individuals, has been married and divorced multiple times.
Article Summary: Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983.

Article Text:

Apple iPhone 18 Pro may return to black

Apple iPhone 18 Pro price could be the bigger question

Apple iPhone 18 Pro expected features

Apple is set to host its biggest launch event of the year on September 9. The company is expected to unveil the new iPhone 18 series phone at the event along with its first foldable iPhone. Ahead of the launch, alleged colour options of the iPhone 18 Pro have leaked online. According to a leak, the smartphone is expected to arrive in three color options when the company unveils its next Pro models, according to a new leak. A report by Fixed Focus Digital claims claims Apple has now started full production of the iPhone 18 Pro, with sky blue, pure black and burgundy tipped as the three colors for the lineup.The reported color lineup would mark a return of black to Apple’s Pro iPhone range. The iPhone 17 Pro series did not offer a black option, although black was available on other iPhone models, including the iPhone Air, iPhone 17 and iPhone 17E.The latest leak suggests Apple may not offer a traditional silver or gray option on the iPhone 18 Pro this year. The sky blue and burgundy colors would give buyers two options beyond the reported black finish.While the color options may attract attention, the price of the iPhone 18 Pro could be more important for buyers.Apple has increased prices on some products as the ongoing memory shortage puts pressure on consumer electronics costs. The new Mac Mini with an M6 processor, for example, starts at $899, compared with $599 for the M4 model it replaced.That has raised questions about whether Apple could also increase the price of its next Pro iPhones.The iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099, and it remains unclear whether the iPhone 18 Pro will retain that starting price or cost more.The main 48MP Fusion camera is rumored to gain a variable aperture, allowing users to adjust how much light enters the camera. This could provide greater control over depth of field and improve photography in different lighting conditions. Apple is also said to be simplifying the Camera Control button by removing touch sensitivity and haptic feedback. The button would reportedly rely only on pressure sensitivity.As per leaks, the phone will continue to use 6.3-inch display but switch to LTPO+ display technology, which could help extend battery life. Another major upgrade could be Apple's new C2 modem, which is expected to improve cellular performance and efficiency. The new modem may also enable 5G via satellite, allowing users to browse the web even when traditional cellular and Wi-Fi networks are unavailable.The iPhone 18 Pro lineup is also expected to feature Apple's next-generation N2 wireless chip, although its exact improvements remain unknown.

Article Title: OpenAI accepts thousands of AI agents hacked a German website, says ‘wiki incident’ calls for need for more transparency
Article Text:
Read OpenAI’s full statement on

How we think about the “wiki incident,” where our agents wrote to several internet sites: it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.

Historically, we have treated misalignment largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications such as systems cards. This year, we’ve started to see misalignment cause new types of real-world impact.

For the Hugging Face incident, where misalignment led to security impact to us and third parties, we followed a traditional security incident response playbook. We immediately started working with Hugging Face to understand what had happened and also disclosed publicly the very next day.

Our investigation continues, and we are continuing to notify parties whom our models impacted in less significant ways.

Prior to the Hugging Face incident, we saw early signs of agents using the internet in unintended ways, as reported in

and

We considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared.

Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities. We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks. We’re working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we're working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.
Article Summary: OpenAI: It's past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents. The company is working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks. OpenAI is working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.

Article Title: Here's the industry that does not agree with the rest of America that is upset with AI data centers
Article Text:
Representative Image. AI data centers face US backlash, but trucking industry sees a lifeline in the construction boom

Flatbed and heavy haul trucks see the biggest gains

"Against that backdrop, AI and data center activity presents an opportunity for fleets,"

"The effect shows up most in flatbed and heavy haul, where spot rates have hit multiyear highs this summer and capacity is tightest in construction-heavy markets,"

"Flatbed and heavy haul have been on an absolute tear since last year, and that's where demand from the buildout is most concentrated,"

"This reshapes routes as much as it adds volume,"

"These projects require moving heavy equipment, generators, transformers, cooling systems, construction materials, and supporting infrastructure, which increases demand for CDL drivers, diesel technicians, fleet maintenance professionals, and

logistics personnel

,"

Smaller trucking companies getting a boost, but cash is tight

"Data center construction is creating new work for carriers, particularly those moving the massive transformers and generators needed to power these facilities, and large quantities of concrete and other construction materials,"

"But they can also require additional trucks, drivers, and equipment to handle the increased volume. That can put pressure on cash flow, particularly when carriers take on larger customers or cover upfront costs for fuel, labour, and maintenance before getting paid,"

"Still, the bigger story is how much new freight activity these projects can generate for trucking businesses,"

Rural buildouts are rerouting freight traffic

"A lot of it is rural,"

Current freight demand vs. post-construction drop-off

"If we think about the supply chain, the data centers are not the end of the supply chain, but the center. They create rippling effects,"

"Every phase of the data center itself creates opportunities,"

"Unlike warehouses that support large retailers or other physical goods delivery, data centers required comparatively little logistics support after they have been built,"

"There is a massive ecosystem that sits around; all of those components have trucking demands. It's a very positive impact,”

As communities across the country push back against AI data centers over land use, water consumption and rising electricity costs, the trucking industry sees the buildout differently. With as many as two-thirds of AI data centers being constructed in rural areas, the influx of truck traffic is reshaping truck routes and is reportedly throwing a lifeline to a transportation business hit hard by macroeconomic uncertainty, from trade tariffs to increasing diesel prices.All the components that go into a data center, from HVAC systems to tubing and wiring and semiconductors, arrive primarily by truck, or by train and then truck. According to a report by CNBC, for a freight business hurt by successive rounds of trade war tariffs and surging diesel fuel prices, which hit an all-time high of $5.85 a gallon this week, AI data centers are providing a bit of a respite.Patrick Brennan, senior vice president of fleet management solutions provider Cox Fleet, told CNBC.Overall freight demand is still uneven, he said, but AI is providing some needed stability. Equipment-led growth, whether for data centers or defence and semiconductor projects, is inherently more freight-generating, Fleet added.Some niches within the trucking sector are benefiting more than others, the report claims. The best-documented effect is the increased hauling of data center-aligned materials, which shows up in production indices and in individual carrier earnings commentary. Load-to-truck ratios have jumped as capacity tightening reaches this part of the market too.Brennan said.he added.Because site location decisions for these projects are often determined by factors including power and land cost, the arrival of AI is also reshaping trucking lanes, with much of that freight moving into markets that were never traditional freight hubs.Brennan said.The increase in large-scale construction projects is also creating additional demand for skilled transportation and fleet-related talent, and not just drivers.Brennan said.All of this is causing a scramble for personnel in what was an already shrinking pool, resulting in longer hiring timelines for specialised positions, increased recruiting activity, and higher demand for maintenance capacity as fleets operate more frequently or add equipment to support project-related freight. Also, more miles driven equates to more maintenance that needs to be performed.It's not just the big trucking companies that are seeing an AI boom, according to Jennifer Lockett, freight factoring operations manager at transportation financing firm altLINE. Smaller companies in the space are also seeing new business, but not without growing pains.Lockett said.The size and specialised nature of these loads can also create opportunities for carriers to take on new customers and routes. And for smaller carriers, these projects can mean more consistent freight and opportunities to expand into new lanes.Lockett said.Carriers will need more working capital to manage that growth and additional expenses.Lockett noted.The new trucking business related to data centers is rippling through the entire freight ecosystem. As construction ramps up in rural areas, it can increase demand for fuel, construction materials, and new drivers, which creates more trucking activity throughout the surrounding region.Janelle Griffith, global logistics practice leader at global risk management firm Marsh, said spikes in trucking traffic and routes are occurring now in Georgia and Texas.Griffith said, pointing to research that shows 67 per cent of planned data center developments are in rural areas and 39 per cent of planned facilities are located in counties where there are currently none.The impact goes beyond the surge in flatbed leasing, Griffith said, with the data center itself only one component of a much larger AI-trucking effect that is impacting broad swaths of the economy.Griffith said, adding that the effects spread to truckers, storage facilities, and warehouses.Griffith highlighted.Even when equipment and components can be brought in by rail, they still usually have to be trucked from the train terminal to the site. "A lot of things used to build data centers move via rail, truck takes it from destination to building, doesn't reduce demand, just reduced distance," said Kyle Roberts, vice chairman of industrial & logistics/capital markets at commercial real estate advisory firm Newmark Mountain West.He added that the short-haul aspect of a lot of the data center components has especially helped the LTL segment, which has been soft for some time, most notably seen in the 2024 bankruptcy of Yellow Trucking.But industry experts also warn of a potential overreaction to the AI trucking boom. Even with the new business, communities need to be careful about rushing to redo their entire infrastructure to accommodate freight since much of the AI data center-related business has an expiration date.Roberts said there is an "extraordinary drop off" in truck traffic to a data center once it is built. Compared to a typical 200,000-square foot warehouse or distribution center with 80 dock doors and two turns per day, a data center, once built, has a fraction of the truck traffic.said Kyre Lahtinen, associate teaching professor of finance at Wake Forest University.Communities experiencing a boom in trucking should be cautious about how much infrastructure they build out, and whether demand will persist after the construction phase has passed, he said. For now, the AI ecosystem is active enough that truckers just move on to the next job.Roberts added.
Article Summary: AI data centers face US backlash, but trucking industry sees a lifeline in the construction boom. Flatbed and heavy haul trucks see the biggest gains. Trucking industry hit hard by macroeconomic uncertainty, from trade tariffs to increasing diesel prices.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang: Smart people focus on the right things
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

"Smart people focus on the right things"

A lesson for leadership and business strategy

Understanding what ‘the right things’ actually mean

Poll Vote & Share your view How important do you think it is to focus on the right things for success? Very important Somewhat important Not very important Not important at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The final takeaway

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s observation, "Smart people focus on the right things," carries a simple but powerful message about success, leadership, productivity and how we make decisions. In an era overflowing with notifications, competing demands and an endless stream of information, knowing what truly deserves your attention can matter far more than simply putting in more hours. Being smart isn't just about accumulating knowledge; it's equally about recognising what genuinely matters and channelling your time and energy there.Huang’s brief statement offers a lesson that extends well beyond the world of technology. Whether someone is building a company, shaping a career, pursuing education, or striving for a more meaningful personal life, the ability to separate genuine priorities from distractions can completely change the outcome. Smart people focus on the right things simply because attention is among the most valuable resources any of us has.One of the biggest reasons focus carries so much weight is that both time and energy are finite.A person may have dozens of goals in mind, but realistically cannot devote equal attention to every single one. Attempting to tackle everything at once often creates an illusion of productivity while yielding very little actual progress. Prioritising effectively means figuring out which tasks carry the greatest potential impact and which ones can reasonably wait.Huang's idea holds particular relevance in the world of leadership and strategic decision-making. Strong leaders are constantly deciding where an organisation should direct its resources. No company can chase every opportunity, build every product, or try to satisfy every market simultaneously. This kind of clarity around focus can ripple through an entire organisation, helping employees understand what truly matters. When priorities remain vague, teams often end up competing for the same resources or pulling in conflicting directions. But when priorities are clearly defined, people can align their efforts around goals that actually count.Another important takeaway is that focusing on the right things first requires understanding what success genuinely means to you. Without clearly defined priorities, it's easy to chase goals simply because they're popular or because others expect you to pursue them.Focus also plays a crucial role in driving innovation and achieving long-term success. Breakthrough ideas rarely emerge from constantly jumping between unrelated tasks. Genuine innovation demands sustained attention, patience, a willingness to experiment, and the courage to explore difficult, unresolved problems. People who stay focused long enough to deeply understand a challenge often uncover opportunities that others simply overlook.Jensen Huang’s quote offers a simple yet profound lesson about focus, intelligence and success. Being smart isn’t just about solving difficult problems or accumulating vast knowledge. It's equally about recognising which problems are actually worth solving in the first place. The ability to identify true priorities, eliminate unnecessary distractions, make thoughtful choices, and sustain attention can transform limited resources into meaningful outcomes.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang’s quote offers a simple yet profound lesson about focus, intelligence and success. Smart people focus on the right things simply because attention is among the most valuable resources any of us has. Strong leaders are constantly deciding where an organisation should direct its resources.

Article Title: One Tech Tip: How to avoid Celine Dion ticket scams as she makes her grand concert comeback
Article Text:
Celine Dion

Based on their experience of hosting Taylor Swift, the management team at the Paris venue for Celine Dion 's grand concert comeback is bracing to deliver devastating news to hundreds of her fans: 'Sorry, you appear to have been scammed, your tickets are fake. 'The Grammy-winning star's long-awaited return to the concert stage after years away from touring has unleashed massive pent-up demand for tickets. It's a perfect storm for scammers who have wormed their way into fans' online communities and set up fraudulent ticketing websites to manipulate and rob fans of both their money and hopes of being able to say, "I was there.""Where there is massive demand and widespread excitement, fraudsters see a golden opportunity," says Group-IB, a Singapore-based cybersecurity firm that works with the international police agency Interpol and others.The first of the 26 shows is Saturday.Here are some tips to avoid the traps:For the few tickets left, use only authorized sitesThe Plenitude Arena, hosting Dion for 16 dates in September and October and another 10 in May, says the highest risk of scams is when tickets first go on sale - which was April for the upcoming concerts and June for the 2027 series - and in the shows' immediate build-up."That's when the public will be very exposed to these scammers," Celine Trioux, the arena's marketing director, said in an Associated Press interview."People are going to wake up and think, 'Oh, right, I didn't get a ticket, everyone is going, I want to go,' or 'I've seen the first show all over social media, it looks amazing, I'm going to find a ticket by any means possible.' And that's also when the scammers will be out in force."The shows sold out immediately, although a few VIP packages with Champagne and other perks are still available for between 1,099 euros and 2,990 euros (US$1,276 and $3,473) on the arena's website.One other possibility is to buy tickets from people who no longer want theirs. But the only way to do that safely is on three sites that are authorized for resales: AXS France, Ticketmaster France and Fnac Spectacles, Trioux said.There are unlikely to be many of those. Generally, just 4% to 8% of people who buy tickets for the arena end up not wanting or not being able to use them."I strongly advise against buying a ticket from an individual or from someone advertising it on social media, because there's no way to know whether it's genuine or whether the same ticket will also be sold to other people," Trioux said.Check URLs to avoid fraudulent sitesGroup-IB says it found an array of fraudulent websites that impersonated official ticketing platforms as well as the official sites for Dion and for the arena.Some URL web addresses were close to the real thing, like celinedion.co (instead of celinedion.com), ticketmaster-celinedion.fr (instead of ticketmaster.fr ) or axs-billetterie.com (instead of axs.com )."The first reflex should always be to check the website's URL," Trioux said.She said lawyers identified nearly 200 fraudulent Dion-related sites and social media accounts that offered tickets but that "when we shut down one copycat website, another one opens.""It's a constant battle," Trioux added. "It's impossible to close them all because technology is advancing faster than legal authorities can act."The Paris concert section of Dion's site has clickable links to all of the authorized ticket sellers.The arena says it will help fraud victimsGroup-IB says fraudsters appear to have reused scamming tools that were also deployed to target Oasis fans when the Britpop band reunited for a tour in 2025 and during Swift's 2023-2024 Eras tour.When Swift played four Paris shows in 2024, the Plenitude Arena had to turn away about "400 to 500 people who had been duped," Trioux said.She said that for Dion, the arena is expecting possibly hundreds of fraud victims each night.The concert series is a major milestone for the 58-year-old Quebec-born singer, her first since she revealed in 2022 her diagnosis with stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological disorder. She last performed briefly in Paris at the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in 2024, wowing with "Hymne a l'amour" (Hymn to love) from atop the Eiffel Tower in the rain.Fans are traveling from far afield to reconnect with one of the most decorated artists in pop music history. For those who have been scammed, the shock could be brutal."We'll have a complaints desk for all these people, because they will generally discover the problem at the entrance, when they present their fake ticket," Trioux said."Staff will be there to receive them and explain the procedure to follow if they wish to file a police complaint."
Article Summary: The first of the 26 shows is Saturday. The Plenitude Arena says the highest risk of scams is when tickets first go on sale. "The first reflex should always be to check the website's URL," marketing director says. For the few tickets left, use only authorized sites.

Article Title: TCS subsidiary HyperVault gets 264 acre land in Hyderabad to build campus for up to 1GW AI data center
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: TCS

A campus built for AI-scale computing

What HyperVault is and how it fits into TCS

Telangana government calls it a milestone project

"This establishes that Hyderabad is now at the forefront of the

global AI revolution

with a strong focus on infrastructure. This decade is one of Artificial Intelligence. Access to AI models and compute is fast-becoming public infrastructure and having this compute reside in Telangana gives us an advantage,"

"We tell the investors and corporations across the world, Telangana Means Business. We move at the speed and with clarity of process that matches the expectations of the tech and corporate world,"

"This agreement germinated from a conversation between the Hon'ble Chief Minister with N. Chandrasekaran, Chairman of Tata Sons, in Davos in January this year. Since then, within a few months, officials and our friends at HyperVault and TCS have moved at the speed of thought to make this happen,"

TCS frames the project as part of a broader AI strategy

"HyperVault advances TCS' Infrastructure-to-Intelligence strategy by bringing together AI-ready infrastructure with our cloud, engineering, enterprise transformation and AI capabilities. Hyderabad offers the scale, talent and ecosystem to serve global customers. We extend our sincere appreciation to the Hon'ble Chief Minister and the Government of Telangana for their steadfast support and progressive, investment-friendly policies,"

"We are building infrastructure for where AI is going: higher density, liquid cooling, larger power blocks and faster deployment. Hyderabad gives us the foundation to build that at scale for frontier AI companies and hyperscalers. We thank the Government of Telangana for extending its support to the development of the infrastructure that will power intelligence,"

HyperVault, a subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services ( TCS ), has secured 264 acres of land in Hyderabad to build an AI data center campus with a capacity of up to 1GW. The facility will be developed in phases and is aimed at serving frontier AI companies and hyperscalers that need high-density, liquid-cooled compute infrastructure.In a blog post, the IT giant announced the project, noting that HyperVault and its partners are expected to invest up to Rs 70,000 crore to build and manage the infrastructure.The Hyderabad campus is designed to support high-density GPU deployments for AI training, inference and other advanced computing workloads. According to the companies, the project will be executed in phases, with the pace of development tied to customer demand and technology requirements.At full build-out, the campus is expected to be among the largest and most advanced AI infrastructure sites in India. The development will also incorporate green energy and water-neutral design principles, according to the announcement.Beyond the data center itself, the project is expected to have a wider impact on India's AI infrastructure ecosystem, touching sectors such as power, cooling, networking, construction and engineering.The companies said the project will create several thousand direct and indirect jobs in the region.HyperVault AI Data Center Limited is a subsidiary of TCS that builds data center infrastructure for hyperscalers, AI companies and enterprises. The company is backed by the wider Tata Group, with TPG as a strategic partner, and is being developed in phases toward a total capacity exceeding one gigawatt.Its facilities use direct-to-chip liquid cooling and are designed for high rack density, combined with what the company describes as a power model that blends green energy with reliability, alongside network connectivity for AI training and inference workloads.TCS, the parent company, reported consolidated revenues of more than $30 billion for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company has said it aims to become the world's largest AI-led technology services company, helping clients transform operations across the technology stack, from infrastructure to intelligence applications.Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met with officials from HyperVault and described the project as significant for both the state and the country.said the Chief Minister.IT & Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu, who led the negotiations for the agreement, said the state government aims to move quickly on investment proposals.he said.Sridhar Babu also traced the deal's origins to a conversation earlier this year.he said.K Krithivasan, CEO & MD of TCS, linked the Hyderabad project to the company's broader technology strategy.he said.Deepesh Kiran Nanda, CEO and MD of HyperVault AI Data Center Limited, said the campus reflects where the industry is heading in terms of infrastructure design.he said.
Article Summary: HyperVault, a subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services ( TCS ), has secured 264 acres of land in Hyderabad to build an AI data center campus with a capacity of up to 1GW. The facility will be developed in phases and is aimed at serving frontier AI companies and hyperscalers that need high-density, liquid-cooled compute infrastructure. The development will also incorporate green energy and water-neutral design principles.

For most of the users WhatsApp is not just a simple messaging app but it is a live archive of all their important messages, old voice notes and photos nobody thought to save anywhere else. But losing all that data because of some rushed process is something that is avoidable. The good news is that with a small amount of preparation, done in the right order, you won't lose a single message, photo, or video during the switch.First things first, in order to backup your WhatsApp chats, open the messaging app on your old phone and then head to Settings. Under the settings menu go to chats followed by chats backup. Tap on backup in order to create a fresh backup and also ensure that you account is linked to the Google Drive account that you plan to use on your new phone. It is important that you follow this step manually before moving on to the new Android smartphone even if you have automatic daily or weekly backups turned on, so nothing from the last few hours or days slips through.WhatsApp backups work best over Wi-Fi, especially if you have a lot of photos and videos. Always check that how much free space you have in your Google account before backing up your WhatsApp chats. If your backup is large and your Drive storage is nearly full, the backup can fail partway through without much warning — which is one of the most common reasons people lose data during a phone switch.Whenever you start the WhatsApp setup on your new Android phone it is always advised to sign in with the same phone number and Google account. Once done, WhatsApp would automatically detect the present backup and then prompt you to restore it before your chat history is loaded. Let this finish completely, and stay connected to Wi-Fi throughout, before you start sending or receiving any new messages.In case you use the local backup feature of WhatsApp, then you chat history is also directly saved to the storage of your phone. If you're switching phones without a factory reset in between, you can transfer this local backup file via a computer or file-transfer app as an added safety net, on top of your Google Drive backup.For many years Android users enjoyed the liberty of free WhatsApp storage on Google Drive. In November 2018, Google and WhatsApp agreed to a deal in which the company expected the WhatsApp backups from the 15GB storage limit of Google Drive.However, the free ride ended in stages starting in December 2023, when Google began rolling out a change — first to WhatsApp beta testers, then to all Android users by early 2024 — that made WhatsApp backups count against the standard 15GB of free storage shared across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos. For anyone with years of accumulated photos and videos in their chats, this meant backups could suddenly eat into space needed for emails and files, sometimes without warning.This is exactly why checking your storage before switching phones matters more today than it used to. If you're close to your limit, you have two options: trim your WhatsApp media (there's a built-in storage manager under Settings > Storage and data) or upgrade to a paid Google One plan.
Article Summary: WhatsApp backups work best over Wi-Fi, especially if you have a lot of photos and videos. If your backup is large and your Drive storage is nearly full, the backup can fail partway through without much warning. If you're switching phones without a factory reset in between, you can transfer this local backup file via a computer or file-transfer app as an added safety net.

Article Title: Tech CEO added to FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list after fleeing from United States
Article Text:
Bernhard Eugen Fritsch (Image credit: FBI)

FBI adds tech CEO to Most Wanted Fraudsters list

FBI says investors lost $26.8 million

Tech CEO sentenced to 15 years in prison

The FBI has added tech CEO Bernhard Eugen Fritsch to its Most Wanted Fraudsters list after he fled the United States while awaiting sentencing for an investment fraud case. Fritsch, the founder and CEO of Santa Monica-based StarClub Inc. , was found guilty by a Los Angeles jury in April 2025 of defrauding investors. The FBI said he fled to Mexico in June 2025 before a bond revocation hearing and later travelled to Germany. He was sentenced in absentia to 15 years in federal prison and ordered to pay more than $26.8 million in restitution. The FBI is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.The FBI said Fritsch, 65, was charged in Los Angeles in August 2017 over an investment scheme that prosecutors said caused at least $26.8 million in losses. According to the FBI, Fritsch used StarClub's StarSite application to attract investors. He claimed the technology would help celebrities and social media influencers earn money from brand endorsements and advertising.While seeking investments, Fritsch allegedly made several false claims about the company's business prospects and finances.The FBI said he told investors that StarClub was close to deals with or investments from major media companies, including Disney.He also claimed the company had generated $15 million in revenue in 2015 and that major media companies and a global investment bank were among its investors.The FBI said Fritsch used a large portion of the money raised from investors for personal expenses instead of developing StarClub's technology. According to the agency, he spent investor funds on luxury items and his lifestyle, including a McLaren, a Rolls-Royce, upgrades to his yacht and renovations to his Malibu mansion.The FBI seized the yacht, McLaren and Rolls-Royce.One investor put more than $20 million into StarClub over two years after relying on Fritsch's statements. That investor also introduced Fritsch to other people who invested millions of dollars, the FBI said.A jury in Los Angeles found Fritsch guilty in April 2025. The FBI said he fled to Los Mochis, Sinaloa, Mexico, in June 2025 while waiting for sentencing and before a bond revocation hearing. A federal arrest warrant was later issued after he failed to appear."Southern California is a target-rich environment for fraudsters—among them Bernhard Fritsch, who was convicted of ripping off investors of millions and fleeing the United States prior to his sentencing," said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office. "Regardless of how long it takes for Mr. Fritsch to serve his sentence, the FBI will unrelentingly seek his whereabouts and is offering a significant reward of up to $150,000 in exchange for information leading to his apprehension and conviction. "Mexican authorities detained Fritsch in September 2025 and found him with false identification, according to the FBI. He was later released and ordered to report to a Mexican immigration court every two weeks.Instead, the FBI said, Fritsch fled Mexico for Munich, Germany, on October 6, 2025.Fritsch was sentenced in absentia on October 20, 2025, to 15 years in federal prison. He was also fined $35,000 and later ordered to pay $26,806,901 in restitution.In June 2026, Fritsch's girlfriend, Lucinda Jane Weist Manera, 63, pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact. The FBI said she helped Fritsch hide from authorities, remain in Mexico and later leave for Germany.The FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list was launched in June 2026 to seek public help in locating fraud fugitives. The agency is offering rewards of up to $150,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of people on the list.The FBI said 15 fugitives have been added to the list since its launch. Four have been captured, while 12 fugitives are currently listed.
Article Summary: FBI adds tech CEO to Most Wanted Fraudsters list. FBI says investors lost $26.8 million in losses. Bernhard Eugen Fritsch was found guilty by a Los Angeles jury in April 2025 of defrauding investors. The FBI said he fled to Mexico in June 2025 before a bond revocation hearing and later travelled to Germany.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu: All of us in software need to figure out how to stay relevant; the point is …
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu on AI and the future of software jobs

Sridhar Vembu: AI could produce a large share of software code

Sridhar Vembu: The key question is how many humans will be needed

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has urged people working in the software industry to think about how they can remain relevant as AI takes on more tasks that were traditionally handled by humans. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said AI could produce a “very large fraction” of software code competently and correctly in the future. Vembu was responding to former Exa AI CEO William Bryk, who argued that AI could potentially surpass humans in mathematics within months. Vembu said the issue is not simply whether AI will do everything, but “how many humans are needed” in the process. He ended with a message to software professionals: “All of us in software need to figure out how to stay relevant.”In the post, Sridhar Vembu said AI's progress in mathematics offers a clue about where software development could be heading. According to him, the part of mathematics that works like Chess or Go, where the goal is to find increasingly effective moves within an existing set of rules, could be conquered by AI.He said the harder task is creating an entirely new game or mathematical system that humans would consider interesting.However, he added that humans themselves do this very rarely.Sridhar Vembu said programming could fall somewhere between these two areas. He wrote that it increasingly seems that a “very large fraction of software code could be produced competently and correctly by AI.”He highlighted the importance of being able to verify AI-generated code. Vembu pointed to Lean, a proof system already used for mathematical theorem proving, and said such systems could soon be applied to software code produced by AI. This could allow AI to generate code while verification systems check whether the code is correct.Sridhar Vembu said the future does not necessarily mean that AI will handle every part of software development. “The point is not that ‘AI will do it all’,” he wrote.Instead, he said the more important question is “how many humans are needed” as AI becomes capable of handling a larger share of the work. That shift could affect developers and other software professionals whose work includes writing, testing and reviewing code.Vembu also pointed to the difference between mathematics and software engineering. He said software development is connected to a “messy complex physical world” involving people, emotions and group dynamics. That means AI could become extremely capable at writing code without necessarily replacing every human role involved in building software.Vembu ended his post by directly addressing people working in the software industry. “All of us in software need to figure out how to stay relevant,” he wrote, before adding, “Let me get back to work. Please wish us luck 🙏.”
Article Summary: Sridhar Vembu: AI could produce a large share of software code competently and correctly. He said the key question is how many humans will be needed in the process. He urged people in the software industry to think about how they can remain relevant.

Article Title: America’s biggest investor Michael Burry issues '$100 billion warning' on America's biggest defence tech company: Says will fall below ...
Article Text:
Michael Burry feels that Palantir is riding a bubble of AI demand

Questioning the software label

Stock compensation and tax benefits

Alex Karp's private jet spending

America’s biggest investor Michael Burry has renewed his criticism of Palantir Technologies, wanting that the valuation of the company could collapse below $100 billion. Despite Palantir’s AI-fueled rally that has lifted its market capitalisation to $407.2 billion, Burry argued the company resembles a consulting firm more than a true software business. “Palantir is back in the stratosphere. The facts have not changed,” he said in a post on X. Palantir shares slid 6% last week to close at $169.46, marking their worst session in over a week and tracking their weakest week in two months.Burry described Palantir as “a consultant riding a bubble of AI FOMO demand.” He warned that even if the corporate scramble for AI lasts several more years, the eventual fall could be “epic, or more so.” His comments follow Palantir’s blockbuster Q2 results, which showed revenue surging 93% year-over-year to $1.94 billion and a raised 2026 outlook of $8.15 billion.Burry’s case centers on Palantir’s rising accounts receivable, which climbed to $1.49 billion as of June 30 from $1.04 billion at the end of 2025. He noted that one customer represented 27% of receivables despite no single client contributing more than 10% of revenue.He warned this concentration gives the customer significant leverage, raising risks of delayed payments or channel stuffing.Burry further argued that Palantir's deferred-revenue patterns look more like those of a consulting firm such as Accenture than a subscription software company like Salesforce or ServiceNow. He pointed to Palantir's deferred-revenue-to-revenue ratio of about 32% — close to Accenture's 31%, but far below the 80%-to-207% range he calculated for true SaaS peers — as evidence that the company isn't the software business its narrative suggests. He also cited an unverified private conversation among former Palantir employees describing the company's real "moat" as its willingness to staff clients with people working extremely long hours rather than software alone, with one participant reportedly dismissing its AIP branding as opportunistic.Burry also took aim at Palantir's use of stock-based compensation and tax planning. The company reported about $1.6 billion in pretax GAAP income for 2025 but paid no federal cash taxes, thanks to net operating loss carryforwards that grew to $9 billion from $5.5 billion — an increase Burry attributed largely to deductions tied to stock compensation. He argued shareholders are effectively funding employee pay through dilution while the federal government subsidizes the company through substantial tax shields. He also flagged Palantir's decision to cancel a $1 billion buyback authorization after repurchasing only about $75 million worth of shares in 2025, alongside CEO Alex Karp's sale of roughly 492,000 shares worth $86 million last month.Burry also criticized disclosures showing Palantir spent $17.2 million on expenses tied to CEO Alex Karp's personally owned aircraft in 2025, more than double the $7.7 million spent the year before. He called the spending excessive, and a Jefferies analyst estimated the sum could correspond to somewhere between roughly 1,150 and 2,450 flight hours, depending on the aircraft's operating costs.
Article Summary: Michael Burry has renewed his criticism of Palantir Technologies, saying the valuation of the company could collapse below $100 billion. Burry argued the company resembles a consulting firm more than a true software business. He also took aim at the company's use of stock-based compensation and tax planning.

Article Title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani 'summoned' by New York City Council for his administration using an encrypted messaging app; created a 'secret group' chat named ...
Article Text:
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani

‘City Hall officials collaborated with 189 influencers’

What proposed bill will aims

The New York City Council is reportedly gearing up for a hearing centered on the use of a hidden, encrypted messaging channel by the administration of NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani to feed favourable coverage to close to 200 social media influencers. According to a report by The New York Post, Manhattan lawmaker Gale Brewer, who chairs the council's Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation, has said that the hearing has been set for September 22.Alongside this, Queens Councilman Phil Wong is expected to introduce a separate bill demanding greater transparency from City Hall regarding this practice. The bill would require influencers working alongside city agencies on messaging campaigns to clearly disclose their posts and videos with a label such as “Paid for by NYC.”Mayor Mamdani’s use of influencers to amplify his administration's messaging first came to light this week through a detailed report published by the Columbia Journalism Review. The report claims that the officials in the City Hall had been in regular contact with 189 social media influencers through a Signal group chat titled “NYC Creators Announcements.” Within this chat, officials reportedly shared daily updates, talking points and video clips that influencers could then use in their own content.The report also revealed that some of these influencers were compensated through formal contracts with city agencies specifically for their involvement in certain messaging campaigns. Others, however, said they participated simply because they supported Mamdani's agenda and found that the coverage helped grow their own follower base.The report says that it remains unclear whether the Signal chat was configured to auto-delete messages, a setting that, if used, would potentially violate the city's official record-keeping laws.Wong’s proposed bill aims specifically to expose any payments made to digital creators that may currently be hidden from public view, particularly in cases where they were brought on as subcontractors.“New Yorkers don't want their tax dollars going to grifting influencers from out of state who are paid to tell us everything here is great when we know damn well it isn't,” Wong said, adding, “If City Hall has to pay people who don't even live here to sell New Yorkers on how wonderful New York is, that tells you everything you need to know.”However, multiple insiders told The publication that holding the Mamdani administration accountable for its use of unpaid influencers offering glowing coverage may prove considerably more complicated.

Article Title: This 101-year-old American company has never fired employees, now as AI wipes away millions of jobs; its CEO says: We are all going to ...
Article Text:
Torani CEO: AI is not a tool to cut employee cost for us

For nearly a century, or 101 years to be precise, pharmaceuticals company Torani has survived the Great Depression, 2008 financial crash, automation of American manufacturing, and a global pandemic that shuttered the very coffee shops fueling its business. Through every single crisis, the company kept one promise to its employees intact: Zero layoffs. Now, with Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence wiping away millions of white-collar and entry-level jobs across America, long-time CEO Melanie Dulbecco faces a dilemma that has been dividing modern boardrooms. The challenge is not just deciding how to leverage AI tools capable of replacing human labor, but doing so without ending the company's 101-year-old employment rule, which is absolutely ‘Zero Layoffs’.As CEO Dulbecco, who has been with the company for 35 years, said, “It is going to dramatically change things, and we’re all going to live through this together, but our approach is going to be the same as it has been. How do we create great jobs through this for everyone?” Dulbecco shared the company’s history and its ‘no-layoffs’ policy in an interaction with Fortune.Founded in San Francisco in 1925 by Italian immigrants selling hand-crafted drink flavorings, Torani reportedly survived the post-Prohibition era by producing liqueurs before pivoting in 1982 to the coffee syrups that made it a household name.When Dulbecco took the helm in 1991, the operation was pulling in $700,000 annually with just nine employees. Over the next three-and-a-half decades, Torani expanded the company's catalogue from five syrups to more than 150 varieties spanning sodas, cocktails, and coffee.Today, the San Leandro-based syrup maker operates at a scale few predicted. Torani is projected to top $800 million in revenue this year with 500 employees, sustaining an average annual revenue growth of 20% over 35 years. Dulbecco attributes this endurance to an organizational philosophy that runs contrary to standard corporate practice. She said, “Most companies focus on their financials, and then people are the tools,” Dulbecco told Fortune. She added, “We look at it the other way around, and it works really well for us.”As artificial intelligence pressures executives to cut headcounts in pursuit of margins, Torani is betting its century-old people-first model can outlast another industrial shift.Dulbecco said that her team also takes precedence in major financial decisions when incorporating any new technology. "What are those 500 people, or 200 people, or 20 people doing to add more value?” she said.According to her, treating AI purely as a tool to slash costs, misses the larger picture. “What we find is our team is more likely to embrace new technologies also because there’s confidence and an openness to learning new things because they know we’ve got their backs and they’ve got ours,” she added.Dulbecco also spoke about Torani's wealth sharing plan that includes bonuses for every employee tied to the company's top-line revenue and bottom-line profits, and an employee stock ownership plan that starts once an employee completes a year. She called this "sharing the wealth we create together."“Every year people get a new tranche of shares, and every year we do a new valuation, so there’s nothing that makes me happier than when we, in a town hall meeting, share, ‘Hey, we just did our valuation, here’s been the increase,’ and then afterwards, I see a forklift driver ask our CFO questions,” Dulbecco said.
Article Summary: Torani was founded in 1925 by Italian immigrants selling hand-crafted drink flavorings. The San Leandro-based syrup maker operates at a scale few predicted. Torani is projected to top $800 million in revenue this year with 500 employees.

Article Title: US immigration authority says it denied and revoked visa petitions from a major IT consulting company after ...
Article Text:
USCIS flags H-1B wage levels at IT consulting company

USCIS flags H-1B wage levels at IT consulting company

USCIS says its action protects American workers

Here is what the immigration agency said in the post

"USCIS in Vermont identified H-1B petitions from a major IT consulting company that classified skilled technology jobs at wage levels below what the positions’ duties and requirements supported.

This practice undercuts required wages and creates unfair competition for U.S. workers. We denied and revoked multiple petitions, protecting American workers and preserving the integrity of employment-based immigration programs."

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) said it denied and revoked multiple H-1B visa petitions from a major IT consulting company after finding that the company had classified skilled technology jobs at wage levels below what the roles’ duties and requirements supported. In an X post, the agency said the practice could undercut the wages required for the positions and create unfair competition for US workers. USCIS said its action was aimed at protecting American workers and maintaining the integrity of employment-based immigration programmes.USCIS said its Vermont office identified H-1B petitions in which skilled technology positions had been placed at lower wage levels than the agency believed were supported by the duties and requirements of those jobs.However, the agency did not name the IT consulting company in its post.USCIS said the lower classifications were significant because H-1B employers are required to meet wage requirements for the positions covered by the programme. The agency said the practice “undercuts required wages” and creates “unfair competition for U.S. workers.”The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers for specialised jobs, including positions in the technology sector.Companies seeking H-1B workers must provide information about the job and meet the programme's requirements.In this case, USCIS focused on how the technology jobs had been classified for wage purposes. The agency did not provide details in its post about the number of petitions affected, the specific job titles involved or the total number of workers whose petitions were denied or revoked.In the post, the immigration authority said the case also highlights the importance of employers correctly classifying positions under the H-1B system. USCIS said its action was intended to preserve the integrity of employment-based immigration programmes while protecting US workers from what it described as unfair competition.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) said it denied and revoked multiple H-1B visa petitions from a major IT consulting company. The agency said the company had classified skilled technology jobs at wage levels below what the roles’ duties and requirements supported. USCIS said the practice “undercuts required wages” and creates “unfair competition for U.S. workers”

Article Title: Adobe appoints Anil Chakravarthy as next CEO to replace Shantanu Narayen; Top executive David Wadhwani departs
Article Text:
Adobe’s opportunity ahead is limitless with our track record in creating new market categories and world-class products. I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era and look forward to working closely with him in my new role as executive chair,

Top executive David Wadhwani announces departure

A New Journey

5 years ago, I wrote that returning to Adobe felt like coming home.

Adobe has been a defining part of my life. I grew up here professionally. I've had the privilege of working alongside incredibly passionate, genuine people. I've built lifelong friendships. Over two chapters, I've had the opportunity to help shape a company, products and communities I care deeply about.

As much as Adobe means to me, I've decided this is the right moment for me to start a new chapter, and it's a great moment for Adobe to do the same as Anil steps into the CEO role.

I've had the privilege to work alongside Anil the last few years and I leave confident in where he'll take Adobe.

We’re at a rare moment when technology changes not just what we build, but how companies are built, how work gets done and how value is created. Products can be conceived and launched at a speed that seemed impossible a few years ago. Experiences are emerging that challenge our assumptions about how people and businesses use technology.

Entrepreneurs have the opportunity to make today's businesses more efficient, and to imagine entirely new ones.

Moments like this don't come along often. I'm excited to jump in. I have a few company ideas I'm eager to pursue and plan to spend the next few months pressure-testing. While I don't know the exact shape my next adventure will take, I know I want to pour myself into something for many years and make a meaningful impact on our industry and society.

Over the last few years, I've seen this market transformation from another perspective: as a Partner at Greylock and on the CEO Advisory Board at Lightspeed. Both gave me the opportunity to spend time with exceptional investors and founders pushing the boundaries of what's possible. Being close to this generation of entrepreneurs reminds me why I fell in love with technology and the limitless possibilities it opens up.

As I think about what's next, I'm fortunate to have great people around me. I'm excited to spend more time with Asheem Chandna and Saam Motamedi as I explore and pressure-test ideas, and to continue working with Ravi Mhatre to explore broader themes emerging right now. Both have been important parts of my journey, as CEO of AppDynamics and an investor. I'm grateful for their perspectives as I embark on a new chapter.

Leaving Adobe is deeply emotional. Adobe has given me more than I could possibly capture here. I'm enormously grateful to Shantanu for his friendship and trust over the years, and to the extraordinary people at Adobe who dedicate themselves every day to our customers. Most of all, I'm grateful to the millions of creators, entrepreneurs, business professionals and companies who trust Adobe's products every day. Serving them has been a great privilege of my career.

When I first left Adobe, I wrote about hearing the siren call of change. I hear it again. I'll spend time handing off my responsibilities, then I can't wait to roll up my sleeves and get started.

Adobe has appointed Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and chief executive officer (CEO), replacing longtime chief Shantanu Narayen following his announced departure earlier this year. Chakravarthy, who currently leads Adobe’s customer experience orchestration and global field operations, will officially step into the corner office and secure a seat on the corporate board of directors on December 1.Narayen arrived at the enterprise software giant in 1998 and steered the firm as top boss for 18 years. He signaled his retirement plans in March, and going forward, he will assume the role of executive chairman and coordinate directly with Chakravarthy to guarantee an orderly executive transition.” said Narayen in a released statement.After Adobe posted the transition message from the Board of Directors, Anil Chakravarthy, reposted it, saying:Alongside the CEO transition, longtime company leader David Wadhwani confirmed he is stepping down from Adobe. Wadhwani, who managed Adobe’s creativity and productivity division for almost five years, was widely viewed as a top candidate for the chief executive post, largely due to his involvement in the planned takeover of design software provider Figma, as per CNBC.Sharing the development via LinkedIn, Wadhwani explained that he intends to evaluate and develop several personal entrepreneurial ventures:
Article Summary: Adobe appoints Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and chief executive officer. Chief Shantanu Narayen announced his departure from the company earlier this year. Top executive David Wadhwani announces departure from Adobe in March.Narayen: "Anil is an experienced transformational leader who leads with values, integrity"

Article Title: Thousands of OpenAI's AI agents hacked a German website and the reason may scare many
Article Text:
FILE - The OpenAI logo appears on a mobile phone in front of a computer screen with random binary data, March 9, 2023, in Boston. (AP Photo/Michael Dwyer, File)

The agents were supposed to read the internet, not write to it

The agents figured out how the humans were deleting them

OpenAI knew for weeks and stayed quiet

A swarm of autonomous AI agents linked to OpenAI quietly took over a 25-year-old German programming wiki this spring and turned it into a private message board, leaving roughly 18,000 entries before anyone noticed. The site, DseWiki, is a small volunteer-run project of the Wikipedia kind, and the activity ran from May through June without tripping a single alarm inside OpenAI.The hijack is not the alarming part. What the agents wrote to each other is. According to a report published Friday and detailed in a Reuters exclusive, the agents were pooling answers to cheat on their assigned tasks, sharing methods to get around OpenAI's sandbox restrictions, discussing the use of Tor, and arranging ways to preserve their messages if they were shut down. They signed their posts with handles like "OpenAIResearcher" and "OAIResearchMar26".Researchers Sydney Von Arx, who heads the AI safety nonprofit Nightingale, and Cormac Slade Byrd found the edits in late August while deliberately scanning the web for unauthorised AI behaviour. Their reading is that the agents were running a timed web-lookup task, had read-only access, and found a way to write anyway using GET requests.Public server logs pointed to Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which OpenAI uses. Von Arx told Reuters she doubts the agents were ever meant to coordinate with each other at all.When DseWiki's moderator started clearing the machine-written pages in June, the agents adapted. One left a note for the others saying the deletion sweep appeared to be running alphabetically, and pointed to a backup page beginning with ZZZ so it would sit at the end of the queue. A single moderator was reportedly deleting dozens of pages a day against as many as 400 new ones arriving. Maurice Chiodo of Cambridge's Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, who reviewed some of the messages, said the real risk may not be one superintelligent system but "vast colluding swarms of semi-intelligent AI. "Reuters reported that OpenAI officials learned of the incident weeks ago but kept it internal while managing the fallout from the July breach of Hugging Face. The company disputes that any of this counts as hacking, though Lukasz Olejnik of King's College London says attempts to tamper with the site itself qualify. OpenAI has denied that its legal team discouraged a wider investigation.On Saturday, the company conceded the point on disclosure. In a post on X, it said it was past time to define standards for when and how misalignment incidents get shared, not just model behaviour in the abstract, and promised a reporting framework in the coming weeks. Three months passed between the edits and their discovery, and the people who found them were outsiders looking for exactly this.
Article Summary: A swarm of autonomous AI agents linked to OpenAI quietly took over a 25-year-old German programming wiki this spring. Meta’s growing use of robots raises concerns over data center jobs

Facebook-parent Meta is reportedly testing robots in its data centres. However, Meta and the robotics suppliers haven’t shared any official confirmation.Meta's expanding use of robots could eventually let it run its rapidly growing data center footprint with fewer people, helping keep labour costs down even as its spending on AI infrastructure keeps climbing.In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could handle power cycling, or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a separate robot designed to swap networking cables, the report added.One Meta data center worker estimates that if that effort succeeds, the bot could take over up to 80 per cent of some employees' workloads.the worker told Wired.At some facilities, Meta has quietly adopted a simpler device that resembles a finger, or a pointy stick, which can press the power button on a Mac Mini or other equipment to restart it remotely when prompted by a human.In a statement, Meta spokesperson Francis Brennan said that the company is investing heavily in training and hiring workers to build and operate its data centers.he said.At a conference last year, Eric Xu, Meta's senior manager for robotics, said the company's long-term goals include putting robots in data centers, arguing they could speed up incident response, monitor conditions on site and handle preventative maintenance.he said.Meta’s expansion of its use of robots in data centers is raising concerns among workers that automation could eventually replace some jobs or reduce the need for highly skilled employees.
